text: Professional OverviewHydraulic engineering focuses on water as its core research object, concentrating on the coordination between the natural movement laws of water (such as precipitation, runoff, evaporation, etc.) and the human society's demand for water (such as water supply, irrigation, power generation, shipping, etc.). Through engineering technical means, it addresses issues such as uneven spatial and temporal distribution of water resources, frequent water disasters, and water ecological protection. It is a comprehensive engineering discipline that takes into account both "benefiting from water" (developing water resources) and "preventing disasters" (preventing water disasters).Training ObjectivesThe training aims to cultivate comprehensive engineering professionals who possess solid basic theories in hydrology, engineering mechanics, soil mechanics, and material mechanics, and master professional skills in hydraulic engineering planning, design, construction, management, and water resources protection. They can engage in engineering investigation, design, construction, research, management, and education in fields such as water conservancy, hydropower, flood control, water resources management, and ecological water conservancy. Students are required to not only understand theoretical analysis but also be able to solve technical problems in water resource development and disaster prevention and mitigation through practical engineering.
